findings.fact: ev/thread is the standard OS-thread API. :n starts asynchronous work; :t carries the numeric job tuple as task ID. No custom native helper is introduced.
Each asynchronous threaded subroutine increments the event-loop listener reference count.
The event loop is not done while its listener count remains nonzero.
The worker VM calls janet_deinit before its threaded subroutine returns.
The POSIX worker posts its completion callback only after the threaded subroutine returns.
Handling that callback decrements the event-loop listener count.
The CLI runs its root through janet_loop_fiber, whose event loop drains those outstanding references.

application_review: The worker is module-level and receives only three numbers. Main keeps the retained tree local. Constructors create fresh mutable arrays; checks read all nodes; no GC settings, arena or free list are used.
scope: Static inspection of the pinned runtime source used to build the measured VM; not a generic thread-library certificate.
